anomalies.anomaly_type: Revenue Drop + Conversion Drop + CPA Spike
anomalies.business_explanation: On May 14-15, all campaigns simultaneously experienced an 89% drop in revenue and purchases. ROAS fell from 1.33x to 0.15x, meaning every rupee spent generated only 15 paise in revenue. CPA increased 667% to ₹4,683 per purchase. This is a systemic issue affecting all campaigns, not a single campaign problem.
anomalies.root_cause_hypothesis: Website checkout failure, payment gateway outage, or conversion tracking pixel failure. The fact that ALL campaigns were affected simultaneously strongly suggests a technical issue rather than a marketing problem.
anomalies.estimated_impact: Revenue lost: ~₹4.6L over 2 days. Spend wasted: ~₹3.9L (spent but not converted). Total opportunity cost: ~₹4.6L in lost revenue.
anomalies.recommended_action: 1. Immediately check website checkout flow and payment gateway status. 2. Verify conversion tracking pixel is firing correctly. 3. Check if any website updates were deployed on May 13-14. 4. If tracking issue, reconcile data and adjust reports. 5. If checkout issue, escalate to tech team immediately.

anomalies.business_explanation: Daily advertising spend increased by 25-26% above the normal baseline on May 24 and May 30. This means ₹50,000 extra was spent per day without a corresponding increase in revenue. The spend spike did not translate into proportionate returns.
anomalies.root_cause_hypothesis: Possible causes: 1) Budget caps were increased accidentally, 2) New ad sets were launched without proper tracking, 3) Algorithm entered a aggressive spending phase due to audience expansion, 4) Promotional period with higher CPMs.
anomalies.estimated_impact: Additional spend: ~₹1L over 2 days. If ROAS remained at normal levels, this should have generated ~₹1.3L in revenue. Actual return depends on campaign performance during this period.
anomalies.recommended_action: 1. Review budget change history for May 24-30. 2. Check if any new ad sets were launched. 3. Verify if the spend increase was intentional (promotion, launch, etc.). 4. If unintentional, tighten budget caps. 5. Monitor ROAS during spend spikes.

anomalies.business_explanation: The Watermelon Range Awareness campaign has been consistently spending 2-8x more per purchase than the average across all campaigns. Over 21 days, this campaign spent ₹3.2L but generated only 22 purchases at an average CPA of ₹6,800. This campaign is burning budget inefficiently.
anomalies.root_cause_hypothesis: This is an Awareness campaign (not Conversions), so high CPA is expected. However, the CPA is still too high even for awareness objectives. Likely causes: 1) Audience too broad (18-34), 2) Creative not resonating with target audience, 3) Low purchase intent for watermelon range, 4) Landing page not optimized for awareness-to-conversion journey.
anomalies.estimated_impact: Spend at risk: ₹3.2L over 21 days. If paused and reallocated to better-performing campaigns at 1.33x ROAS, potential revenue: ₹4.3L vs actual ₹44K. Opportunity loss: ~₹3.8L.
anomalies.recommended_action: 1. Pause this campaign immediately. 2. Reallocate budget to Tinted_SPF or VitC_Serum campaigns which have 2x+ ROAS. 3. If awareness is strategic, reduce budget by 50% and narrow audience to 25-44. 4. Refresh creatives with stronger value proposition. 5. Set CPA cap at ₹2,000.

anomalies.business_explanation: On April 14, the Watermelon Range Awareness campaign's Broad_18-34 ad set spent ₹11,733 to acquire just 1 purchase. This is nearly 8x the average CPA and represents extremely poor efficiency. The campaign spent ₹11,733 in a single day with minimal return.
anomalies.root_cause_hypothesis: Possible causes: 1) Very small audience pool leading to auction pressure, 2) Creative fatigue after running for 2+ weeks, 3) Audience saturation - same people seeing ads repeatedly, 4) Algorithm exploring new audience segments with low intent.
anomalies.estimated_impact: Spend wasted: ~₹10,263 (spend minus expected value at normal CPA). This single day's inefficiency cost more than 17 days of normal operation.
anomalies.recommended_action: 1. Immediately set daily budget cap of ₹5,000 for this ad set. 2. Refresh creatives - same ad running for 2+ weeks causes fatigue. 3. Exclude past purchasers from audience. 4. Test new audience segments (25-44, interest-based). 5. Consider pausing if CPA doesn't improve within 3 days.

anomalies.business_explanation: The Video_Viewers_LAL ad set within Watermelon Range Awareness consistently shows CPA 2-4x higher than average. This lookalike audience based on video viewers is not converting efficiently. The audience may have watched videos but has low purchase intent.
anomalies.root_cause_hypothesis: Lookalike audiences based on video viewers often have lower intent than purchase-based lookalikes. Video viewers may be browsing casually rather than actively shopping. The 1% lookalike may be too broad.
anomalies.estimated_impact: Spend at risk: ₹1.5L over the analysis period. If reallocated to purchase-based lookalikes, potential improvement: 40-50% reduction in CPA.
anomalies.recommended_action: 1. Test 3% lookalike instead of 1% for higher quality. 2. Create lookalike based on purchasers instead of video viewers. 3. Reduce budget allocation to this ad set by 30%. 4. Test different creative angles emphasizing product benefits over awareness.
